A total of `r RECORDS_N` three-component vibration records measured during site blasting were processed and verified, yielding `r RECORDS_N_COMPONENTS` component histories with consistent acceleration, velocity, and displacement. For `r RECORDS_N_META` records the contractor reported the blast distance and charge; that subset spans distances of `r formatC(min(RECORDS_META$D), format = "f", digits = 0L)` to `r formatC(max(RECORDS_META$D), format = "f", digits = 0L, big.mark = ",")` m and charges of `r formatC(min(RECORDS_META$Q), format = "f", digits = 0L)` to `r formatC(max(RECORDS_META$Q), format = "f", digits = 0L)` kg, and bounds the observed operating conditions.

Using these observations—supplemented outside the monitored range by the amplitude database compiled by the author across different projects (S11D source)—a statistical learning model was fitted that predicts peak particle velocity and acceleration, by component and resultant, for any distance--charge combination within the observed domain. Performance was measured solely on observations excluded from each fit: $R^2$ of `r formatC(EXEC_R2_PPV[1L], format = "f", digits = 2L)`--`r formatC(EXEC_R2_PPV[2L], format = "f", digits = 2L)` for PPV and `r formatC(EXEC_R2_PPA[1L], format = "f", digits = 2L)`--`r formatC(EXEC_R2_PPA[2L], format = "f", digits = 2L)` for PPA over `r EXEC_N_PAIRS` pairs per response, with physical-unit errors of `r formatC(EXEC_ERR_PPV[1L], format = "f", digits = 0L)`--`r formatC(EXEC_ERR_PPV[2L], format = "f", digits = 0L)` mm/s and `r formatC(EXEC_ERR_PPA[1L], format = "f", digits = 1L)`--`r formatC(EXEC_ERR_PPA[2L], format = "f", digits = 1L)` g per component. Coupling among responses improved every prediction relative to the uncoupled model, and the residuals of that verification defined the p50, p90, and p95 prediction levels.

With the p90 targets, the demand suite was calibrated: `r EXEC_SC_N` scenarios covering the `r formatC(EXEC_SC_D[1L], format = "f", digits = 0L)`-to-`r formatC(EXEC_SC_D[2L], format = "f", digits = 0L)` m and `r formatC(EXEC_SC_Q[1L], format = "f", digits = 0L)`-to-`r formatC(EXEC_SC_Q[2L], format = "f", digits = 0L)` kg grid, each containing the `r EXEC_SC_RPS` measured histories scaled to the PPV targets of its condition and rotated to the analysis directions. The suite comprises `r formatC(EXEC_SC_REAL, format = "d", big.mark = ",")` three-component realizations of acceleration, velocity, and displacement, with their response spectra and intensity measures, and is ready for the dynamic deformation model and the liquefaction analysis.

The reliability evaluation is formulated: the probability of failure for each performance criterion, conditioned on the scenario, will be estimated by comparing the calculated demands with the admissible capacities. Its quantification requires the responses of the deformation model and the capacities and criteria of the geotechnical model; until those inputs are available, the study reports no probabilities of failure and no acceptability conclusions.
